title: Deterministic simulation and acceptance
statement: Let $M$ be a finite deterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $x$ be a binary string and $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $M$ computes the Boolean indicator of $L$ on $x$ within $t$ steps, with output the one-bit string giving whether $x\in L$. Then every length-$t$ choice sequence of the associated nondeterministic machine halts on $x$, and $x\in L$ if and only if that machine has a length-$t$ choice sequence whose run halts with output exactly the one-bit string $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite deterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$L$ is a language of Boolean strings
$M$ computes the indicator of $L$ on $x$ within $t$ steps
